text: Understanding Git branching is essential for modern software development. A branch lets you work on new features without affecting the main code. Developers often create feature branches to build and test changes safely. When the work is ready, they merge the branch back into the main project. Before merging, teams usually open pull requests so others can review the code and suggest improvements. This version control workflow keeps the project organised and reduces mistakes. By using branches, merging, and pull requests together, teams can collaborate smoothly and keep their code stable while still developing new ideas.
